subject: Quick update and advice
text: After your last message I checked the schedule again. Things look simpler now. The client pushed the launch to late August, so that buys you breathing room. My advice is to stop trying to nail every detail today. If something is only nice to have, park it. Focus on the three parts that make the pitch work: clear timeline, clean mockups, and a short answer for why this change is worth it. People get nervous when they have extra time, and they start fiddling with colors or fonts. That's fine, but save it for the end. If you hit a snag, call me tomorrow instead of burning an evening over it. I know you like to sort stuff solo, but a second set of eyes can save hours. Also, if the vendor quote comes in high, don't panic. Ask for the itemized list first. Sometimes they pad it with unneeded services. You've got the right instincts here. Just trust the work you've already started, keep your notes tidy, and don't let the tiny stuff crowd out the big picture. We'll be fine. One more thing, if the deck feels heavy, cut a page. It feels scary, but a tight message hits harder than a long one. Send me the version when it's rough, not when you think it's polished. I'd rather help you shape it early than fix the point later. And put a little reminder in your phone. The morning chaos is real. Small check-ins beat big last-minute scrambles.
